topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and states what students should learn about cancer treatment.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how local treatment can remove or destroy tumours and why its success depends on tumour location and spread.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how cytotoxic chemotherapy kills cancer cells and why its effectiveness is constrained by toxicity and resistance.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how blocking essential hormonal signals can suppress breast and prostate cancer growth.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how missing cell cycle checkpoint proteins create vulnerabilities that treatments can exploit selectively.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inhibiting one DNA repair pathway selectively kills cancer cells already deficient in another.

topics.label: Oncogene-directed therapy and kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how identifying the oncogenic driver of a tumour enables treatment directed at its activated kinase.

topics.label: Resistance and limitations of kinase inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine why kinase inhibition can fail to provide durable, tolerable cancer control.

topics.label: Antibody-directed cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibodies recognising cancer cell surface proteins can direct therapeutic effects towards those cells.

topics.label: Evidence for immune surveillance against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic evaluates whether the body's existing immune system protects against cancer development.

topics.label: Immune checkpoint inhibition and tumour recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how reactivating T cells can produce tumour responses that depend on recognition of tumour neoantigens.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells towards cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapies designed to give T cells targeted contact with cancer cells rather than relying on naturally occurring tumour recognition.

topics.label: Treatment challenges and personalised strategies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers how matching treatment to individual tumour characteristics can address variable responses and evolving resistance.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how prevention and earlier detection contribute to observed improvements in cancer outcomes.

topics.label: Future treatment priorities and ethical dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider how future cancer treatment should advance while balancing established survival benefits against toxicity and the uncertainty of new therapies.
